articles.title: An Indian Founder Just Bet $30 Million That Microsoft Office Needs to Be Rebuilt From Scratch
articles.excerpt: Bhavin Turakhia's Neo is an AI-native enterprise platform designed to replace, not upgrade, the workplace software stack. He's bootstrapping it himself.
articles.image_caption: Bhavin Turakhia, serial entrepreneur and founder of Neo, Zeta, and Directi
articles.nri_angle: An Indian serial entrepreneur with a $2 billion track record is taking on Microsoft and Google head-on — a signal that Indian founders are no longer limiting their ambitions to domestic or fintech plays.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TSMC Is Raising Chip Prices Again. Every Device You Own Will Feel It.
articles.excerpt: The world's dominant chipmaker is hiking 3nm prices by up to 15 per cent as AI demand overwhelms supply. Its $165 billion Arizona expansion is a year ahead of schedule.
articles.image_caption: TSMC's Fab 12B semiconductor manufacturing facility in Tainan, Taiwan
articles.nri_angle: TSMC makes the chips inside every device Indian tech workers use and invest in — from Nvidia GPUs to iPhones. The price hikes affect AI startup costs, consumer electronics, and India's own semiconductor ambitions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic Just Hired the Co-Creator of AlphaFold. It Wants to Discover Drugs, Not Just Chat.
articles.excerpt: The Claude maker is building wet labs, launching a dedicated science platform, and targeting diseases that Big Pharma won't touch. An IPO looms.
articles.image_caption: AlphaFold's protein structure predictions revolutionised biology — Anthropic now wants that same approach applied to drug discovery (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India is the world's pharmacy for neglected diseases — exactly what Anthropic is targeting. Indian researchers dominate computational biology, and Anthropic's IPO is a key investment event for NRI tech investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Ransomware Gang Just Leaked Apple's iPhone 18 Pro Secrets From a Tata Factory. India Is Investigating.
articles.excerpt: The breach exposed supplier lists, component designs, and drop-test photos of unreleased iPhone models — threatening the trust at the heart of Apple's India manufacturing bet.
articles.image_caption: Apple's headquarters in Cupertino — a ransomware attack on partner Tata Electronics leaked confidential iPhone 18 Pro designs from an Indian factory
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin Apple engineers face supply chain trust fallout; NRI investors in Tata stocks now price in IP security risk as Make in India's credibility is tested.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nvidia Doesn't Just Want to Sell You GPUs Anymore. It Wants a Cut of Your Revenue, Too.
articles.excerpt: The chipmaker's new revenue-sharing model with AI cloud providers — including India's Yotta Data Services — creates a recurring income stream while lowering the barrier for cash-strapped AI startups.
articles.image_caption: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose company is expanding from hardware sales into recurring AI cloud revenue
articles.nri_angle: Indian AI startups gain access to Nvidia's top-tier GPUs through Yotta Data Services' inclusion in the DSX programme; NRI engineers building dual-geography AI ventures benefit from India-based compute at scale.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Every Big Tech Giant Wants a Data Centre in India. The Government Just Made It Tax-Free Until 2047.
articles.excerpt: Microsoft is committing $17.5 billion, Google $15 billion, and even OpenAI is scouting sites. India's data centre capacity could grow tenfold in a decade — and its zero-tax policy is the reason the world is showing up.
articles.image_caption: Server racks inside a modern data centre facility
articles.nri_angle: Pichai's Google and Nadella's Microsoft are leading the biggest infrastructure bet on India in a generation — creating thousands of high-skill jobs, investment opportunities in data centre REITs, and a new reason for NRI engineers to consider returning.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pichai's Google Just Admitted Its Climate Goals Are Slipping. Amazon's Numbers Are Worse.
articles.excerpt: Sustainability reports released this week show Google's emissions up 25 per cent and Amazon's up 16 per cent in a single year. The AI data centre buildout is burning through net-zero pledges faster than anyone expected.
articles.image_caption: Google server racks inside one of the company's data centres
articles.nri_angle: Pichai's Google and Jassy's Amazon are the two largest employers of Indian tech workers in the US, and both are now building massive data centres in India — raising questions about whether India's own water-stressed, coal-heavy grid can handle the AI buildout without repeating these environmental mistakes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and Japan Just Signed Their Biggest Tech Pact in a Decade. Semiconductors Are at the Centre.
articles.excerpt: PM Modi and Japan's Takaichi sealed agreements on AI, chip manufacturing and critical minerals — with Japanese firms already partnering with Tata Electronics to build India's semiconductor supply chain.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who signed bilateral agreements with Japan's PM Sanae Takaichi on AI and semiconductors
articles.nri_angle: Japan's commitment to India's semiconductor ecosystem — from ROHM's silicon MOSFETs to Tokyo Electron's packaging technology — could create thousands of high-skill engineering jobs, offering NRI chip professionals a viable 'return to India' path for the first time.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Intel's Former Chief Architect Just Raised $60 Million to Build a GPU That Doesn't Need Nvidia.
articles.excerpt: Raja Koduri's Oxmiq wants to license AI chip blueprints the way Arm licenses phone processors. Samsung, MediaTek and Pegatron are backing the bet.
articles.image_caption: A high-performance GPU chip — Raja Koduri's startup Oxmiq raised 0 million to build a licensable GPU architecture that challenges Nvidia's dominance in AI computing
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-origin semiconductor veteran is leading one of the most ambitious AI chip startups in Silicon Valley — a signal that Indian engineers are not just running Big Tech but founding the companies that could reshape its supply chain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft and Tata Are Laying a 3,600-Kilometre Cable Under the Indian Ocean. The AI Race Demands It.
articles.excerpt: The I-2SEA submarine cable will connect India's data centre clusters in Hyderabad and Chennai to Singapore, promising the lowest-latency AI corridor in the region by late 2029.
articles.image_caption: A submarine communications cable being laid — Microsoft and Tata Communications are building the 3,600-kilometre I-2SEA cable under the Indian Ocean (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The cable lands at Machilipatnam — the same Andhra Pradesh coast where Google and Meta are building data centres — and will power the AI cloud services that NRIs in Southeast Asia and India increasingly depend on for work and daily life.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tesla Just Had Its Best Quarter in Two Years. Wall Street Sold It Anyway.
articles.excerpt: Record Q2 deliveries of 480,126 EVs crushed estimates by 20%. The stock dropped 7.5%. For NRI investors riding two years of declines, here's what the numbers actually say.
articles.image_caption: Tesla Model Y, the company's bestselling vehicle that drove the bulk of Q2 2026 deliveries
articles.nri_angle: Tesla is among the most widely held stocks by Indian-American retail investors. The Q2 beat-and-drop pattern offers a case study in sell-the-news dynamics that NRIs with TSLA in their portfolios should understand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Central Bank Told Parliament: Don't Legalize Crypto. Not Now, Not Yet.
articles.excerpt: The RBI warned the Standing Committee on Finance that virtual digital assets threaten India's economy and should remain outside the formal financial system — even as the country leads the world in crypto adoption.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, where the central bank's crypto stance was formulated
articles.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs hold crypto assets and face uncertainty over India's regulatory direction. The RBI's stance directly affects repatriation, taxation, and the viability of crypto-linked fintech investments tied to India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pichai's Google Just Put an AI Agent on Your Mac. It Sorts Your Files, Books Tables and Orders Groceries.
articles.excerpt: Gemini Spark turns Google's chatbot into a desktop automation tool that touches local files — a first for any major AI assistant. Apple, whose own Siri now runs on Gemini, is watching.
articles.image_caption: Google CEO Sundar Pichai at a company event in 2023
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin CEO Sundar Pichai's latest move puts Google ahead in the AI agent race, with implications for Indian engineers at Google and Indian SaaS companies competing in the automation space.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: South Korea Just Bet $591 Billion on Chips. India's Semiconductor Dream Looks Like a Rounding Error.
articles.excerpt: Samsung and SK Hynix will build new mega-fabs, double memory chip output and race to own the AI supply chain. India's $10 billion chip mission has a long way to go.
articles.image_caption: A semiconductor wafer used in microelectronics manufacturing
articles.nri_angle: For NRI investors tracking semiconductor stocks and Indian engineers working at Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron, South Korea's massive bet reshapes the global chip map — and raises hard questions about India's own fab ambitions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Every AI Lab Wants Its Own Chip Now. The Race to Dethrone Nvidia Just Got Three-Way.
articles.excerpt: Anthropic is in talks with Samsung to build a custom 2nm processor. OpenAI already taped out its inference chip with Broadcom. For Indian semiconductor engineers, the shift from buying GPUs to designing bespoke silicon opens a new frontier.
articles.image_caption: Nvidia's dominance in AI chips faces a mounting challenge from Google, OpenAI, and Meta developing their own custom silicon (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian chip-design engineers are being heavily recruited by AI labs building custom silicon, and India's semiconductor mission benefits from the industry's push to diversify manufacturing away from TSMC.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Central Bank Just Called AI the Biggest Cyber Threat to Banking. Here's What That Means for Your Money.
articles.excerpt: The RBI's latest Financial Stability Report flagged AI-enabled attacks as the most important near-term risk. With UPI processing 757 million transactions a day and NRI deposits exceeding $140 billion, the warning hits close to home.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building in Kolkata
articles.nri_angle: NRIs maintaining NRE/NRO/FCNR accounts in India face direct exposure as the RBI mandates banks upgrade to AI-speed defences against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats targeting cross-border transactions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's AI Job Paradox: Hiring Surges 16% Even as IT Giants Slash Thousands
articles.excerpt: AI roles are booming, GCCs are scaling fast, and TCS wants as many AI agents as employees. Traditional IT workers face a reckoning.
articles.image_caption: TCS Chairman N. Chandrasekaran at the India Economic Summit. He recently said AI agents may soon equal TCS's employee headcount.
articles.image_credit: World Economic Forum / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in IT services face an urgent reskilling imperative; GCC leadership roles offer reverse-brain-drain opportunities for diaspora professionals with AI + domain expertise.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's AI Startup Funding Explodes 317% — Here's Where the Smart Money Is Going
articles.excerpt: AI startups raised $676 million in the first half of 2026 while overall startup funding declined. Sarvam's unicorn round and Google-Accel co-investments mark a turning point.
articles.image_caption: India's AI startup ecosystem attracted $676 million in the first half of 2026, a 317 percent year-on-year surge driven by sovereign AI ambitions and global investor appetite.
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors can access Indian AI startups at significantly lower valuations than US counterparts; Accel-Google program explicitly courts diaspora founders bridging India-US tech corridor.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Why Every Fortune 500 Wants an AI Hub in India: GCCs Cross 2,100 and Half a Million Hires
articles.excerpt: Global Capability Centres are no longer back offices. With $84 billion in revenue and two-thirds of new roles requiring AI skills, India's GCCs are becoming the innovation engines of the world's biggest companies.
articles.image_caption: International Technology Park in Whitefield, Bengaluru — one of India's premier tech corridors housing major IT firms and Global Capability Centres.
articles.nri_angle: NRI professionals can access global-mandate leadership roles at India GCCs; real-estate ecosystem around tech corridors offers investment opportunity tied to India's AI-driven economic transformation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's IT Sector Has Lost a Third of Its Value This Year. The Next Two Weeks Will Tell If It's Over.
articles.excerpt: TCS reports July 9, Infosys follows, and the Nifty IT sits at a five-year low. With AI eating into margins and global tech budgets frozen, India's $250 billion software industry faces its hardest reckoning since the dot-com bust.
articles.image_caption: The glass pyramid at Infosys Electronic City campus in Bengaluru
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors hold significant positions in Indian IT stocks, and millions of Indian tech workers depend on the health of TCS, Infosys, and HCLTech — making the Q1 results deeply personal for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple's New Siri Runs on Google's Brain. In Europe, It Runs on Nothing.
articles.excerpt: Tim Cook held 'constructive' talks with EU regulators this week as Apple's Gemini-powered Siri AI remains blocked across the bloc — a standoff that could reshape AI regulation globally.
articles.image_caption: Apple CEO Tim Cook
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of Indian engineers at Apple and Google built the Siri AI features now blocked in Europe, while the EU precedent could influence India's own draft AI governance framework.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta Wants to Sell Its Spare AI Compute. It Just Spooked the Entire Chip Sector.
articles.excerpt: A report that Meta plans to become a cloud computing provider sent semiconductor stocks tumbling — SK Hynix fell 15%, CoreWeave lost $7.5 billion — while SoftBank announced its own AI cloud venture the very next day.
articles.image_caption: Mark Zuckerberg, CEO of Meta Platforms, whose plan to sell spare AI compute capacity spooked the chip sector
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors are heavily exposed to the semiconductor boom — Micron gained 240% last quarter alone — and the overcapacity fears directly affect India's own chip buildout plans in Gujarat and Dholera.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft and Amazon Just Bet $3.5 Billion That They Can Replace Your IT Consulting Firm
articles.excerpt: Both cloud giants launched enterprise AI deployment armies within 48 hours of each other. For TCS, Infosys, and the rest of Indian IT, the forward-deployed engineer era is a reckoning and an opportunity.
articles.image_caption: Satya Nadella, CEO of Microsoft, whose company launched a $2.5 billion AI deployment venture
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT services firms that employ hundreds of thousands of H-1B professionals are directly threatened by Microsoft and Amazon building in-house deployment arms — but the FDE hiring boom could also create thousands of new high-skilled roles for Indian engineers in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SK Hynix Wants $29 Billion From Nasdaq. It Could Be the Largest Tech Listing in a Decade.
articles.excerpt: The South Korean chipmaker that supplies Nvidia's AI memory is about to go public in the US. For Sanjay Mehrotra's Micron and India's semiconductor ambitions, the stakes just went up.
articles.image_caption: The Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square, New York, where SK Hynix plans to list in what could be the largest tech IPO in a decade
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors and Indian semiconductor professionals in the US can invest directly in AI's most critical memory supplier via Nasdaq ADRs, while the listing intensifies competition for Micron's India fab in Gujarat.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Just Offered the US Government a 5% Stake. It Wants Every AI Company to Do the Same.
articles.excerpt: Sam Altman has pitched Trump, Bernie Sanders, and the Treasury Secretary on a sovereign wealth fund seeded by AI equity. Anthropic says it's not interested.
articles.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman at a meeting in February 2025
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin AI professionals face equity dilution; White House AI advisor Sriram Krishnan is central to the talks; India's sovereign AI ambitions must now account for partially government-owned American competitors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: HCLTech Just Won a $1.14 Billion AI Deal in Europe. Indian IT's Worst Year Might Be Turning.
articles.excerpt: The contract is entirely new business — not a renewal — and lands as the sector trades at five-year lows. Earnings season starts next week.
articles.image_caption: HCLTech's SEZ campus in Noida, one of the company's major global delivery centres
articles.nri_angle: HCLTech employs tens of thousands of Indian professionals on H-1B and L-1 visas; the deal signals that AI is transforming, not eliminating, IT services jobs; NRI investors face a critical earnings season with IT stocks at five-year lows.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Persistent Systems Just Bid $1.4 Billion for a German Firm. Indian IT's Europe Bet Is Getting Serious.
articles.excerpt: The Pune-based company's takeover of Munich's Nagarro would be the largest European acquisition by an Indian mid-tier IT firm, as the industry hedges against American visa uncertainty.
articles.image_caption: Frankfurt's central business district, Germany's financial hub where Nagarro trades on the stock exchange
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT firms are building European delivery capacity as an alternative to H-1B-dependent US operations, giving Indian tech workers more transfer options beyond North America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Data Centres Are Eating the World's Memory Chips. Your Next Phone Will Cost More.
articles.excerpt: A 90% surge in DRAM prices is rippling from data centres to consumer electronics. Retailers are warning of 'inevitable' price rises, and India's semiconductor ambitions just got a new rationale.
articles.image_caption: A data centre server room — surging AI infrastructure demand is driving DRAM and NAND prices higher, raising costs for consumer electronics (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI consumers in the US and India face rising electronics prices as AI demand drives chipflation, while India's domestic semiconductor mission gains strategic urgency.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Washington Banned an AI Model for Two Weeks. The Fallout Is Just Starting.
articles.excerpt: The US government's emergency export controls on Anthropic's Fable and Mythos models have created a de facto approval regime for frontier AI — and a new risk factor for the industry's biggest IPOs.
articles.image_caption: The United States Capitol in Washington, D.C., where lawmakers are grappling with AI model export controls (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian researchers at US AI labs were directly affected by access restrictions, while India's sovereign AI startups like Sarvam stand to benefit from growing demand for non-American AI infrastructure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Concentrix Lost a Quarter of Its Value This Week. India's Call Centre Industry Is Next.
articles.excerpt: The American outsourcing giant's stock crashed 24% after it warned that AI is eating into its business. With 1.65 million BPO workers in India, the shockwave is heading east.
articles.image_caption: Concentrix corporation headquarters — the business-process outsourcing giant lost a quarter of its market value after warning that AI is eroding demand for its services
articles.nri_angle: Indian BPO workers face the sharpest edge of AI displacement, and NRI investors holding IT services stocks should reassess exposure to the outsourcing sector.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ShareChat Just Turned Profitable. Now It Wants $400 Million From Public Markets.
articles.excerpt: India's homegrown social media platform, once burning through venture cash, has hit operational profitability and plans an IPO within five quarters. The secret weapon: 700 million micro-drama episodes watched daily.
articles.image_caption: The ShareChat app — the Indian-language social platform turned profitable in FY2025 and is now preparing for a $400 million IPO (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: ShareChat's IPO gives NRI investors a rare chance to bet on an Indian-built social platform competing directly with Meta and YouTube in the vernacular content space.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oracle Cut 21,000 Jobs Last Year. Nearly Half Were in India.
articles.excerpt: The database giant spent $1.84 billion on severance while tripling its capital spending on AI infrastructure. Its latest annual filing says the hardest part hasn't started.
articles.image_caption: Oracle Corporation headquarters in Redwood City, California
articles.nri_angle: Oracle employs tens of thousands of Indian engineers in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and on H-1B visas in the US. With 10,000 of its 21,000 cuts falling on India, the restructuring directly reshaped the Indian tech job market.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zuckerberg Just Admitted Meta's AI Bets 'Haven't Come to Fruition.' The Stock Fell 5%.
articles.excerpt: At an internal town hall on Thursday, the Meta CEO said AI agent development has been slower than expected and that the restructuring which cost thousands of jobs was not as clean as it should have been.
articles.image_caption: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg at the White House in September 2025
articles.nri_angle: Meta employs thousands of Indian engineers on H-1B visas and runs major AI research operations in India. Zuckerberg's admission that the AI agent thesis hasn't materialised raises questions about whether the layoffs and team reshuffles that displaced Indian workers were premature.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sanjay Mehrotra's Micron Just Posted $41 Billion in a Single Quarter. The AI Memory Shortage Is That Bad.
articles.excerpt: The IIT Delhi alumnus delivered the most explosive earnings report in semiconductor history, with revenue up 346 percent and margins wider than most software companies.
articles.image_caption: Sanjay Mehrotra, CEO of Micron Technology and co-founder of SanDisk
articles.nri_angle: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, born in Kanpur and an IIT Delhi alumnus, leads a company building a semiconductor facility in Gujarat — India's first major memory chip investment — while delivering record-breaking earnings driven by AI demand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Palantir's CEO Just Called OpenAI a 'Wealth Tax.' Indian IT Stocks Had Their Best Day in Weeks.
articles.excerpt: Alex Karp's attack on token-based AI pricing sent enterprise software stocks soaring — and gave India's battered IT sector its first real relief in months.
articles.image_caption: Palantir CEO Alex Karp at an AI summit
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT stocks — held widely by NRI investors and employing hundreds of thousands of Indian engineers — rallied 4.64% on the back of Palantir CEO's attack on AI labs, offering the first major relief for a sector down 25% this year.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Ransomware Gang Just Leaked Apple's iPhone 18 Pro Secrets. The Breach Came Through India.
articles.excerpt: More than 200,000 files stolen from Tata Electronics have exposed supplier lists, component designs, and photos of Apple's unreleased flagship — raising hard questions about India's manufacturing security.
articles.image_caption: Apple's headquarters in Cupertino, California — a ransomware breach at its Indian manufacturing partner Tata Electronics leaked iPhone 18 Pro design documents
articles.nri_angle: Tata Electronics is central to India's Make in India push and assembles 25% of global iPhones — the breach tests whether India's manufacturing ecosystem can be trusted with the world's most valuable supply chains, a question that matters to NRI investors in both Apple and Tata.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nvidia Is Tired of Selling Shovels. Now It Wants a Cut of the Gold.
articles.excerpt: Jensen Huang's new revenue-sharing model turns Nvidia from a chip seller into a cloud landlord — a bet that its thousands of Indian engineers and NRI shareholders are watching closely.
articles.image_caption: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
articles.nri_angle: Nvidia employs thousands of Indian engineers across Santa Clara, Bangalore, and Hyderabad — the revenue-sharing pivot could change how the market values the company and directly affects NRI investors who have ridden NVDA's stock through a frustrating 2026.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
